messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rolling v2.4.1 -> green in us-west-2. Canary traffic 5% (staggered across AZs). Watch: healthchecks=enabled, dns-ttl=30s.

maria (eng): seeing 502 spikes in the canary group for us-west-2a. Alerting on request failures.

oncall-bot: P1 page sent to kevin (on-call) — incident created: INC-2026-0289 (latency + 5xx increase).

kevin (on-call): acknowledged. Pulling logs + LB config. Anyone touch the envoy service mesh or nginx layer?

chris (sre): I flipped a config last night but only in us-west-2b, not 2a. Not related to rollout but could interact.

maria (eng): stack traces show upstream write timeout: 'upstream prematurely closed connection' from inference-proxy -> runtime. Sample curl from canary:```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD' https://us-west-2.api.redwood.ai/gen -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}'
* Connection #0 to host us-west-2.api.redwood.ai left intact
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream_connect_failed","detail":"connect() failed (111: Connection refused)"}```

product-ops: CS flagging customers on calls. Which tenants mapped to canary? any high-traffic ones?

customer-success: A handful of early-adopter customers routed to the canary (3 enterprise tenants). They report intermittent failures and degraded throughput. Impact estimate: ~8-12% of API calls in us-west-2 are failing.

kevin (on-call): ok. Tentatively this looks like a bad model-serving variant in the green pool. Two mitigation options: (A) kill canary routing (stop sending new requests to green) or (B) rollback to blue (cancel staging rollout). Which is quicker?

maria (eng): kill-switch for routing can be done in ~30s via feature flag: `ffctl set rollout.v2.4.1.enabled false --scope=us-west-2` — that stops new traffic to green, existing in-flight may still fail.

chris (sre): DNS is low-ttl but we have some clients honoring previous IPs; kill-switch at router level safer. I can run an immediate drain on green instances if we abort.

kevin (on-call): do it. Maria, flip the feature flag. Chris, start drain and block green from registering to LB. Maria/kevin coordinate rollback if kill doesn't reduce errors in 2 minutes.

maria (eng): running: `ffctl set rollout.v2.4.1.enabled false --scope=us-west-2 --reason "canary 502s"`

maria (eng): :white_check_mark: flag set. Monitoring.

chris (sre): initiating drain: `infractl instance-state set --tag v2.4.1 --state DRAINING --region us-west-2` — this will stop new connections to green nodes.

kevin (on-call): watching metrics... error-rate dropping from 11% -> 4% in last 40s. Good sign. Latency trends stabilizing.

product-ops: initiating customer comms draft for affected tenants. Will send interim note: "we identified an issue with a canary deployment and have stopped traffic — you may see transient failures; engineers are monitoring."

customer-success: Please add impacted tenant IDs: tenant-A, tenant-B, tenant-C. They need ETA.

maria (eng): still seeing a couple of timeouts from long-polling sessions — likely in-flight requests that hit already-failed workers. Those should clear within a couple minutes.

kevin (on-call): if errors <2% in 3 minutes, we keep kill-switch and mark incident as mitigated. If not, prepare full rollback: `redwoodctl rollout cancel --region us-west-2 --id v2.4.1 --force` (this will flip traffic back to blue).

chris (sre): drain progressing. 85% of green sockets closed. No new registrations.

maria (eng): logs show model binary in green hitting a memory limit on some instances — probably regression from quantized build. We'll create a postmortem.

kevin (on-call): customer impact: product-ops please confirm. product-ops: what does CS want me to tell customers?

product-ops: send this: "We detected errors for a small % of traffic in us-west-2 after a canary deploy. We've stopped the canary and drained affected hosts; requests should recover. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."

customer-success: sending to tenants now. They asked for roll-back ETA — "monitoring, ETA ~10-15m until we confirm full recovery".

kevin (on-call): error rate now down to 1.1% and trending down. I'll keep incident open for postmortem and handoff. Oncall rotation: maria is taking over monitoring for next 30m then chris will do a deep dive. I'm removing myself from pager at 09:00 UTC — handoff to maria.

maria (eng): acknowledged. I'll maintain watch, collect logs and the failing model binary hash. Adding a snippet: `sha256sum model-v2.4.1-quant.bin = ab12...ef34` for tracing.

chris (sre): I'll follow up to check whether the quantization pipeline introduced a regression — scheduling debug run on staging with the same flags.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused: v2.4.1 (us-west-2) — reason: operational pause by kevin (on-call).

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0289 severity: P1 -> mitigated (customer impact reduced). Please fill incident template and link logs.

product-ops: filing incident ticket and preparing internal RCA. Add note: "partial blue/green canary failed due to model memory regression in quantized build; kill-switch prevented wider impact."

customer-success: Tenants confirmed services recovering. One tenant saw 30s sustained disruption before recovery. They're asking for credit; routing to accounts.

maria (eng): creating postmortem branch: `gitlab.com/redwood/infra/incident-inc-2026-0289` and will attach logs + model hashes + rollout timeline.

kevin (on-call): handing off to maria (eng) for watch and postmortem. If errors reappear, page me. Closing my active on-call message.

maria (eng): taking over. I'll post a short summary in #incidents and ping product for customer-facing RCA draft.

chris (sre): once postmortem confirmed, we'll block this quantization flag on automated rollouts until explicit sign-off.

maria (eng): :mag_right: root cause draft: quantized model introduced an edge-case memory spike on some host types; combined with staggered blue/green and low-ttl DNS caused partial user impact. Remediation: disable automated rollout for quantized builds, add pre-rollout mem tests, improve kill-switch docs.

product-ops: thanks team. Closing notes: mitigated, customers notified, postmortem in progress.

kevin (on-call): :thumbsup: final — leaving thread.

maria (eng): last check at 1902345900: 5xx rate = 0.3% (normal). Marking incident status: monitoring -> postmortem.
